brief: A planter tower for a patio: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall, with a crescent of five one-storey planters hugging the front of the ring on the side nearest the default view, so the whole build steps up one, two and three storeys away from the viewer. All bins radial-drain. Behind the ring, three one-storey cells with covers make a potting shelf: one small nursery pot on each cover, each filled with soil and planted with a seedling. Fill every planter with soil and plant it: a patio tomato in the middle; butterhead lettuce, oakleaf lettuce, parsley, basil, chives and a marigold around the ring; nasturtium, alyssum, strawberry, thyme and oregano along the crescent. Use look to check that every plant is visible from the default view.

finish.summary: Built a stepped hex planter tower: a 3-storey central column with a radial-drain bin at its top, six 2-storey ring columns each with a radial-drain bin, five additional 1-storey radial-drain planters, and three covered 1-storey shelf cells with soil-filled nursery pots and seedlings. All 12 planter bins were soil-filled and planted with the named crops, and all shelf pots were filled and planted. check_build is clear. However the five 1-storey planters do not all form a front crescent: three hug the front/south side (-1,2, 0,2, 1,1) while thyme and oregano are at -1,-1 and 0,-2 on the far side, so the intended 1-2-3 crescent stepping from the default view is only partially realised; the shelf is likewise to the east/north-east rather than strictly behind the ring.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, radial holes
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
